Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

and Valencia were absent. Also present were Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Arnold M.

Councilmember Ramirez, Vice Mayor Rios, and Mayor Perez. Councilmembers Ayala

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Mayor Perez highlighted the Walk Groundbreaking and thanked Primestor, Community
Development, Communications and Public Affairs, Public Services, and Recreation and
Park Services for making the event successful; thanked Social Services and all who
attended the Angel Project Recognition Night, recognizing volunteers and sponsors;
reported on her attendance at the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors meeting
where they voted to add a tax measure to the June election which will increase sales tax
by a half cent; shared that the Cultural Arts Center always goes above and beyond in all
they do; encouraged residents to report potholes; reminded them to bring in their trash
cans after trash pickup and indicated the meeting would be adjourned in memory of
Chaplain Benito Richard Garcia and Juan Contreras Gomez. Addressing City Council
was Angelo Maldonado, American Legion Commander, who spoke about Chaplain
Garcia. Vice Mayor Rios wished all a Happy Lunar New Year; reported on her attendance
at Norwalk High School where she spoke to the Economics and Government Club
students regarding the City and government processes; and requested the meeting be
adjourned in memory of Rogelia Lozano.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

City Council proclaimed February as Black History Month in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

Mr. Gomez provided a brief presentation regarding the current storm updates; reported
on his attendance at the Steering Committee for Hermosillo Park; and shared upcoming
“Know Your Rights” workshops with Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights of Los
Angeles. Videos were shared highlighting The Walk Groundbreaking and the “Bi-Weekly”
review.

SUBJECT: PARTICIPATE IN AN AGREEMENT FOR THE LOS ANGELES REGION –
  IMAGERY ACQUISITION CONSORTIUM 8 PROJECT

Background:

The Los Angeles Region Imagery Acquisition Consortium (LARIAC) is a consortium of the
County of Los Angeles (County) in partnership with cities, agencies and academic institutions
and others. Collaboratively the consortium acquires digital remote sensing data, including
imagery and elevation data. The LARIAC8 Project will deliver highly accurate digital aerial
imagery and elevation datasets to local, state and federal agencies at substantial cost savings.
To ensure the accuracy of the aerial imagery the County is working with the consortia members
to plan and initiate the next LARIAC cycle January 1, 2026 – December 31, 2028. The cost of
LARIAC8 for the City is $27,850, paid in two equal installments of $13,925. The first payment is
due Spring 2026, and the second payment is due Spring 2027.

Various departments will benefit from this resource and facilitate planning and management of
multiple citywide projects. The LARIAC8 benefits include high quality image data that enables
staff to make virtual site visits. Some examples include improving site plan review, understanding
impacts of new projects, and a consistent view of the City. The enhanced resolution shows
greater detail and provides more information than other online providers. There are multiple
access methods, including desktop, handheld, and mobile as well as local and remotely hosted
solutions.

Fiscal Impact:

Funds for the first payment are included in Fiscal Year 2025/26 Adopted Budget and the second
payment for Fiscal Year 2026/27 will be requested in the upcoming budget cycle.

SUBJECT: AGREEMENT FOR RECREATION FURNITURE/DESIGN SERVICES

Background:

As part of the Recreation and Park Services Department’s organization and multi-departmental
workspace improvements, the Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex (NASC) and the Cultural Arts
Center (CAC) are being redesigned to create a more collaborative and functional office
environment. The updated layout will accommodate existing staff and visitors, improving shared
workspaces, public waiting areas, storage solutions, and technology access.

Following research, staff selected Sierra School Equipment Company through the OMNIA
Partners cooperative purchasing agreement, which allows the City to “piggyback” off
competitively bid contracts to streamline procurement. The proposed project includes space
planning, design schematics, project management, labor, delivery, and installation of modular
office furniture including cubicles and storage cabinets. The total amount of the agreement is not
to exceed $330,800.

The proposed agreement with Sierra School Equipment Company is in an amount not to exceed
$330,800. The Recreation and Park Services Department has allocated funds in the Norwalk
Arts and Sports Complex Equipment Replacement Fund in the proposed Fiscal Year 2025/26
operating budget.

Rehabilitation Zones 2, 9, and 29. The work scope involves CM&I of improvements to asphalt

signing, striping, loop detector replacements and traffic control.

Engineering to provide labor compliance and geotechnical material special testing services
throughout the duration of the project construction phase. The scope for material testing includes
field monitoring and laboratory testing on base and asphalt materials to ensure compliance with
the project specifications.

Throughout the construction phase, unanticipated delays and rework required additional material
testing services. To ensure compliance with the project specifications for the remaining duration
of the project, staff recommend the approval of Amendment No. 2, in the amount of $109,764 to
provide the required material testing services.

SUBJECT: ADVISORY BODY APPOINTMENTS

Background:

With the exception of the Planning Commission (which is commensurate with the appointing
Councilmember’s term) and five members of the Art in Public Places Commission (which is
established in the Norwalk Municipal Code), Advisory Body terms are for two years following a
City election. Advisory Body terms are from January 1, of odd years to December 31, of even
years.

There are vacancies on several Advisory Bodies: Art in Public Places (3), Community Promotion
(1), Historical Heritage (8), International Friendship (1), Parks and Recreation (3), Public Safety
(5), Senior Citizens (1), Social Services (1), and the Youth Commission (14). The Youth
Commission has one member at this time. The age range for the Youth Commission is between
13 to 18 years of age. Each City Councilmember has three appointments.

Two of the vacancies on the Art in Public Places Committee are appointed based on Norwalk
Municipal Code §15.44.060, and require consensus of the entire City Council. Any
Councilmember may nominate an individual who falls into one of the two categories:
Business/Community College Representative and at-large Community Representative.
